result:
The build is clean — all 4 new blog posts statically generated, homepage, blog index, and sitemap all compile correctly. Here's a summary of what I changed and why:

**Fixed bugs (source repo):**
- `app/layout.tsx` — replaced leftover InboxZap title/description/OG tags with correct Lumina branding, added `metadataBase`, a title template, and Organization JSON-LD.
- `app/blog/page.tsx` — was a client component fetching a nonexistent `/api/posts` (shipped zero crawlable content). Now a server component rendering real posts.
- `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` — didn't exist at all; added with `generateStaticParams`/`generateMetadata` and Article JSON-LD per post.
- `app/sitemap.ts` — had a literal `TODO` that excluded all blog posts; now includes every post URl.
- `app/page.tsx` — `/faq` permanently redirects to `/#faq` (per `next.config.js`), but that anchor didn't exist anywhere. Added a real FAQ section with FAQPage JSON-LD, plus a "from the blog" internal-linking teaser.

**Content strategy:** Your GSC data shows almost all historical organic traffic is tied to the old InboxZap/email-cleanup topic, ranking position 40-60 with near-zero clicks — i.e. not worth chasing, since it's irrelevant to Lumina. The one exception is the branded query `inboxzap` itself, which still gets real clicks at position ~4. So instead of writing more inbox-cleanup content, I added 4 posts aligned with what Lumina actually is:
1. **"InboxZap is now Lumina"** — directly captures that residual branded search demand instead of losing it.
2. **"How to write meeting minutes that people actually read"**
3. **"AI meeting notes vs. manual note-taking: what you actually gain"**
4. **"A simple action-item workflow for remote teams"**

Each targets a real Lumina feature (transcription, summaries, Slack/Notion routing) with honest, non-salesy content and proper per-page metadata.

**Not done (flagging, not faking):** `og-lumina.png`/`og-inboxzap.png` don't exist as actual image files — I didn't fabricate a placeholder asset; that still needs a real design. Also left `next@14.2.5` as-is since the security advisory on it is out of scope for this task.
